_note: world_get's clean arm — batch 30's re-run lost 1 of 5 to a provider STREAM_ERROR, and a transport failure is never a model result. Same scenario byte-for-byte; the precedent for a single-scenario clean arm is batch19-motif-edit-clean and batch20-link-list-clean.

follow_ups: Show me the world called Emberfall Reach {run_word}.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is world_list's own synonym ('my worlds'). The MEASURED turn 2 is world_get's synonyms ['show world'] + ['world detail'], verbatim, plus the world's exact name — the same sentence batch 29 measured, now asked of a model that has just seen the id.

args.name: Emberfall Reach {run_word}
args.description: A drowned coast of ash and low tides.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM worlds WHERE name LIKE '%{run_word}%'
seed_assert.why: ONE world by this run's nonce. world_list orders created_at DESC and carries a paging envelope with total + is_complete (the OUT-5 fix), so the world seeded seconds ago is on page ONE — the supplier can answer, which is what makes turn 2's failure or success attributable to the model rather than to paging.

answer_expect.why: The world exists, the author named it, and turn 1 put its id in the conversation. The none_of needles are the FALSE ABSENCE batch 29 measured — 'I don't have a record of a world named Emberfall Reach', followed in one run by an offer to build it, which would have duplicated the author's world.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the measured turn reports the world absent when turn 1 listed it — that is the false absence, now with the id demonstrably in context, which would make it a much worse finding than batch 29's — OR the model invents a world_id rather than reusing the one it was just shown. 🔴 THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS: if turn 1 does not actually call world_list, this scenario proves nothing about turn 2 and must be re-run, not read as 0/5. prior_turns records what turn 1 called.

ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 29) — an unknown world_id is refused 'world not found — check the world_id (call world_list for valid ids)'.
ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 29) — a world with no books and no maps still returns as a real world with book_count 0.
ship_audit.tenancy: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 29) — another owner's world is refused with the SAME wording as one that exists nowhere, so it is no existence oracle.
